# FitClinicMD

> Telehealth clinic offering physician-guided weight management and hormone
> therapy. Patients are evaluated by licensed providers by video; when
> clinically appropriate, medication is prescribed and fulfilled by a partner
> compounding pharmacy. Cash-pay; no insurance is billed.

## Key facts

- Care is delivered by providers licensed in the patient's own state.
- Treatment is prescribed only when a licensed provider determines it is
  clinically appropriate. A prescription is never guaranteed.
- Compounded medications are prepared by a licensed pharmacy and are not
  FDA-approved products.
- This marketing website collects no health information. Medical intake happens
  only inside the secure patient portal at app.fitclinicmd.com.
- This service is not for emergencies. Call 911 in an emergency.

## Pages

- /how-it-works: the four-step process from intake to delivery
- /treatments: conditions and therapies offered
- /treatments/weight-management: provider-supervised GLP-1 weight management
- /treatments/hormone-therapy: physician-guided hormone therapy, including TRT, guided by bloodwork
- /treatments/peptides: peptide therapy — individual peptides and proprietary blends, prescribed only after evaluation
- /pricing: cash pricing and what is included
- /providers: how our clinicians are licensed and credentialed
- /faq: common questions

## Education (Learn)

Plain-language, non-promotional articles. Compounded medications are not
FDA-approved; individual results vary; nothing here is medical advice.

- /learn: education hub index
- /learn/storing-your-peptide-medication: how to store and handle peptide medication
- /learn/why-results-vary: why two people respond differently to the same peptide
- /learn/compounded-medication-explained: what compounding is and what "not FDA-approved" means
- /learn/peptides-and-hormone-therapy: how hormones and peptides differ and fit together
- /learn/mitochondrial-peptides-explained: what mitochondrial peptides (MOTS-c) are; evidence is largely preclinical
- /learn/what-a-telehealth-visit-involves: what a telehealth visit actually involves
- /learn/why-your-labs-matter: why bloodwork is required before some treatments
- /learn/reading-a-subscription-before-you-sign-up: how recurring billing and cancellation work
